portal_hypertension.title: Beyond Hemorrhage: A Case of Acute Dengue Infection Presenting with Budd-Chiari Syndrome and Bilateral Sensory Polyneuropathy.
portal_hypertension.authors: Dalvi KK, Khaire P, Shaik MH

portal_hypertension.abstract: Budd-Chiari syndrome (BCS) is a rare hepatic vascular disorder characterized by hepatic venous outflow obstruction with an incidence of 1-2 per million population annually. While dengue fever is primarily associated with hemorrhagic complications, thrombotic events are rarely reported. To our knowledge, this represents the first documented case of BCS occurring in association with dengue fever. A 22-year-old male from a rural area presented with a 4-day history of abdominal pain, fever, vomiting, and loose stools. Physical examination revealed hepatomegaly, ascites, and mild dehydration.
